done_state: A read-only facade opens the warehouse, checks v_atlas_status before answering anything (distinguishing never-run, failed-run, and checks-evaluated=0 from a genuinely clean run -- the MAJOR-1 principle applied at this layer), refuses every request when the run is not genuinely clean with a reason naming which state it is in, and otherwise serves reads only from the declared set of gated views, never a raw table, matching ARCHITECTURE.md section 8's stated guarantee that primary enforcement of the trust gate lives here.

criteria.statement: The facade's connection to the warehouse is genuinely read-only -- a write attempt through it raises, not merely a convention the facade's own methods happen to honor.
criteria.verification: atlas/query/tests/test_readonly.py: opens a facade against a migrated warehouse db, attempts an INSERT through the facade's own connection, asserts it raises sqlite3.OperationalError (SQLite's real read-only-connection error).

criteria.statement: status() returns a structured result distinguishing four states that must never collapse into each other: never-run (no ingest_run rows at all), a run whose own status is not 'ok', a run that IS 'ok' but recorded zero dq_check_run rows (checks_evaluated=0 -- the MAJOR-1 vacuous-pass case), and a genuinely clean run (status='ok', checks_evaluated>0). A real per-source contract failure no longer collapses a run out of 'clean' at this layer (ARCHITECTURE.md section 8 addendum, amendment A1) -- that dimension is scoped to fetch()'s own per-view refusal (C4/C12), not status()'s run-level classification. Corrected 2026-09-20, same pass as C4: this criterion's own prior text still required global contract_failures=0 for 'clean', directly contradicting C4's corrected per-source design -- found by Alice during ATLASSN-103 implementation, missed when C4 was first corrected.
criteria.verification: atlas/query/tests/test_status.py: four separate fixtures, one per state, each asserting status() returns the correct, distinct classification -- most importantly that checks_evaluated=0 is never reported the same way as a genuine clean pass, and that a real per-source contract failure alone (checks_evaluated>0, status='ok') now reports clean at this layer, not FAILED_RUN (test_run_ok_with_checks_but_a_real_contract_failure_is_failed_not_clean, updated by ATLASSN-103 to assert the corrected behavior).

criteria.statement: fetch() only permits reading from the 18 views declared in ARCHITECTURE.md section 16 -- a request naming a raw table (e.g. hook_verdict directly) or any name outside that declared set is refused with a clear reason, never silently allowed.
criteria.verification: atlas/query/tests/test_fetch_allowlist.py: fetch('hook_verdict') and fetch('not_a_real_view') both raise a facade-specific refusal naming the requested name; fetch('v_gate_proven_live') against a clean run does not raise.

criteria.statement: When status() is not genuinely clean at the run level (NEVER_RUN, FAILED_RUN, or CHECKS_NOT_EVALUATED), fetch() refuses EVERY request system-wide, unchanged. Within a genuinely clean run, a contract-failure refusal is scoped per-source (ARCHITECTURE.md section 8 addendum, ATLASSN-103, amendment A1): fetch() refuses a specific view only when a source that view's own declared dependency map (A2) names is unqueryable -- not a global contract_failures sum. A source with zero dq_check_run rows for the anchor run is absent from v_queryable_source, not clean, so the vacuous-pass case needs no separate handling. Supersedes this criterion's own prior text, which described the pre-fix global behavior; corrected 2026-09-20 per Owen Reyes's design-scope gap finding (Build 8 backlog authorship) -- the prior wording stated the CURRENT pre-fix behavior as the criterion itself, which is exactly backwards for design-scope criteria meant to gate the fix.
criteria.verification: atlas/query/tests/test_fetch_allowlist.py: for each of the three non-clean run-level states, fetch() against any real view name still raises a run-level refusal, unchanged. New: a fixture with a genuinely clean run where exactly one source (e.g. tessera_event) has a real contract failure -- fetch() against a view whose dependency map (A2) does not name that source succeeds; fetch() against a view that does name it refuses, and the refusal names that specific source and its failing check count (A2).

criteria.statement: When the run is genuinely clean, fetch() against a real gated view returns rows identical to a direct SQL SELECT against the same view.
criteria.verification: atlas/query/tests/test_fetch_allowlist.py: loads a fixture with a clean run and real hook_verdict data, asserts facade.fetch('v_gate_proven_live') returns the same rows as a direct 'SELECT * FROM v_gate_proven_live' on the same connection.

criteria.statement: fetch_live() serves the live plane's views under their OWN freshness gate, and the existing fetch() path is unchanged: with the warehouse deliberately in a non-clean batch state, fetch() still refuses all 18 of its declared views and fetch_live() still serves subagent rows. Neither method will serve a view name on the other's allowlist.
criteria.verification: atlas/query/tests/test_readonly.py and test_fetch_allowlist.py: assert the 18-name ALLOWED_VIEWS set is byte-identical to what it was before this change, assert fetch('v_subagent_tool_call') raises QueryRefused, assert fetch_live('v_hook_verdict') raises QueryRefused, and assert fetch_live serves rows while status() reports failed-run.

criteria.statement: fetch_live() refuses when the live plane's own gate is not open -- never-run, live-pull-failed, live-pull-stale, live-credential-hit -- and the refusal names which state, so a caller can tell 'the pull is dead' from 'a secret was found' from 'nothing has run yet'. The connection stays mode=ro; nothing in the query component ever triggers a pull.
criteria.verification: atlas/query/tests/test_readonly.py drives each live_state and asserts the refusal message names it. A write attempt through the facade's connection raises, as it already does for fetch().

criteria.statement: v_git_commit_detail (ARCHITECTURE.md section 39) is added to query's ALLOWED_VIEWS and served under the same fetch()/status() gating as every other view (C3/C4/C5) -- refused identically to any other gated view when status() is not clean; when clean, returns real rows via LEFT JOIN of git_commit to git_commit_file (not INNER -- the toy-modeled correction from architecture), author_hash only (never a raw author field, per D8), with NULL insertions/deletions preserved rather than coerced to 0. Traces to ATLASSN-98/REQ-77.
criteria.verification: atlas/query/tests/test_git_commit_detail.py (new): fetch('v_git_commit_detail') against a fixture containing (a) a commit with files, (b) a commit with zero git_commit_file rows (must appear with file_path/insertions/deletions all NULL, not silently dropped), (c) a file row with NULL insertions/deletions (must stay NULL). A real range query against the live warehouse cross-checked against a direct `git log --oneline | wc -l` for one project (ATLASSN-98 acceptance criterion 2) -- any discrepancy explained in closing evidence, not ignored.

criteria.statement: No column or join in v_git_commit_detail resolves a commit to a Claude Code session_id. An implementation adding one (even framed as 'one more column' under router pressure, per section 39's own named risk) violates this criterion, not merely exceeds scope. Traces to ATLASSN-98/REQ-77.
criteria.verification: The view's SQL definition and its ALLOWED_VIEWS registration are checked for any session_id-bearing column or join target at implementation and at every subsequent stage close; grep for `session_id` in the view definition must return nothing.

criteria.statement: A malformed or missing commit record (e.g. a git_commit_file row whose parent git_commit row does not exist, or vice versa) is handled by a named, tested rule -- never silently dropped or a crash. ATLASSN-98's own acceptance criterion 5, scoped as this criterion's ablation/negative-control at implementation per PDP.md section 3's design-scope clarification (real ablation fixtures at implementation discharge this, not a non-author prose pass at this stage).
criteria.verification: A real ablation fixture at implementation: a deliberately orphaned git_commit_file row (no matching git_commit) and a deliberately malformed row (missing file_path) each produce a named, observed outcome (reject-and-log or a stated default), proven by a real corrupted-input test before being trusted.

criteria.statement: git_commit gains a v_source_freshness row (confirmed absent today -- checked live against the real view definition during architecture falsification), so ingest staleness for this source becomes checkable the same way every other source already is (ATLASSN-98 acceptance criterion 4).
criteria.verification: SELECT against v_source_freshness after implementation includes a row for git_commit with a real staleness_minutes value, using the same UNION-ALL pattern the view already uses for its other five sources.

criteria.statement: A per-source contract-failure refusal names the blocking source(s) and their failing check counts, pulled from v_source_trust -- not a generic refusal message. ARCHITECTURE.md section 8 addendum, amendment A2. Diagnosability is half of what this fix exists to give a caller (the router), not a side effect.
criteria.verification: atlas/query/tests/test_fetch_allowlist.py: fetch() against a view blocked by a single failing source raises a refusal whose message contains that source's name and its real failing-check count read from v_source_trust, not a placeholder or a generic string.

criteria.statement: The five trust-plumbing views (v_atlas_status, v_pipeline_selfcheck, v_queryable_source, v_snapshot_publishable, v_source_trust) map to the empty source set and stay servable under a contract failure, still behind the run-level gate (C4). v_atlas_status additionally self-describes a never-run state and is servable for that state too. ARCHITECTURE.md section 8 addendum, amendment A3.
criteria.verification: atlas/query/tests/test_fetch_allowlist.py: with a real contract failure present, fetch() against each of the five plumbing views succeeds (not refused); against a never-run (empty) warehouse, fetch('v_atlas_status') succeeds and reports the never-run state rather than raising.

criteria.statement: The declared per-view dependency map (A2) carries a drift test: each ALLOWED_VIEWS member's real transitive base-table closure, recomputed from sqlite_master at test time, equals the declared map (modulo the five plumbing views and A2's source_table translation). Every ALLOWED_VIEWS entry has a map entry -- an unmapped view refuses fail-closed, and the drift test itself catches the omission rather than leaving it as undefined behavior. ARCHITECTURE.md section 8 addendum, amendment A4.
criteria.verification: A real drift test recomputes each view's transitive base-table closure from live sqlite_master and asserts equality with the declared map (an actual comparison, not a hand-eyeballed read, per this project's own PDP R2 discipline). A deliberately unmapped ALLOWED_VIEWS entry (ablation) is confirmed to refuse rather than silently pass, and the drift test itself fails on a hand-edited map that no longer matches the schema.

failure_criteria.statement: fetch() returns data (or an empty result silently indistinguishable from 'no rows') when status() is not genuinely clean, rather than raising a distinguishable refusal.
failure_criteria.detection: Every non-clean status() state has its own fetch()-refuses test (C4); a refusal must be a raised, named exception type, never a quiet empty return.

failure_criteria.statement: A view/table count or allowlist size in this component's code comments or commit messages has no reproduction path.
failure_criteria.detection: grep the component's source and commit messages for numeric claims; each must name the command or test that produced it.

failure_criteria.statement: The facade assumes the warehouse database file exists and is a valid ATLAS schema, rather than reporting a named failure when it is missing or unmigrated.
failure_criteria.detection: Opening a facade against a nonexistent or unmigrated db path produces a named, observable error, not an unhandled exception with no context.

failure_criteria.statement: A refused query is logged to a channel nobody reads instead of being raised to the caller who can act on it.
failure_criteria.detection: Every refusal is a raised Python exception with a message the caller/test directly asserts on -- never a bare print or a swallowed condition.

failure_criteria.statement: v_git_commit_detail uses INNER JOIN (silently drops the 6 real zero-file-row commits) instead of LEFT JOIN, or coerces NULL insertions/deletions to 0, or exposes a raw author/session_id column.
failure_criteria.detection: C8's three-fixture test (with-files, zero-files, NULL-insertions) plus C9's session_id grep -- both must hold simultaneously.

out_of_scope: Foreman's periodic pattern-detection consumer itself (D12 in ARCHITECTURE.md) -- unbuilt and undesigned per the architecture document; this component only provides the read facade a future consumer would use.
The dashboard's specific query needs (D9) -- dashboard gets its own criteria once it is rewired against this facade.
Real end-to-end queries against the live warehouse populated by real ingest/resolve runs -- this component's tests use synthetic fixtures; end-to-end correctness is foreman:integration-test's job.
A general arbitrary-SQL escape hatch -- fetch() is restricted to the declared view allowlist by design (C3), not a general query() that accepts caller-supplied SQL against arbitrary tables.
constraints: Zero third-party dependencies -- Python 3 stdlib only (sqlite3), matching this environment's established convention.
The warehouse connection is opened in SQLite's real read-only URI mode (file:...?mode=ro), not merely a connection the facade's own code promises not to write through.
Tests use Python's stdlib unittest, matching every other component's own convention.

amendments.from: 5 criteria (C1-C5); one gated read path over the batch pipeline's 18 views
amendments.to: 7 criteria (C1-C7); C6-C7 add a second read path with its own gate for the live plane
amendments.reason: ATLASSN-27 / ATLASSN-29. The batch trust gate certifies 19 data-quality checks over hook_verdict, tessera_event, audit_event and git_commit. None of them examines a subagent transcript. Gating the live view on it would mean an unrelated batch failure blinds a parent to its own subagent -- which is not hypothetical: the warehouse is non-clean on fail_open_not_double_counted right now, so every gated view is currently refused. The existing gate is not weakened; a second, differently-contracted one is added beside it. The alternative -- write real dq checks for the live plane and fold it under fetch() -- is named with its cost in DECISION-ATLASSN-27.md.
